name: math_change_of_variables

VINIT.justification: the initial state before a coordinate system or variable is assigned

TANCH.justification: the scalar result that bounds and completes the transformation process

AFWD.justification: the forward transformation function g mapping u to x

AREV.justification: the pull-back operation mapping x back to u

CLINK.justification: the nesting of the transformation within the integrand f(g(u))

IMSCRIB.justification: the recognition that the integral value remains invariant under change of variables

FSPLIT.justification: the separation of the original differential dx into the derivative g'(u) and the new differential du

FFUSE.justification: the product of the derivative and the new differential reconstituting the original measure

EVALT.justification: the successful preservation of orientation during the variable shift

EVALF.justification: the inversion of limits requiring a sign change in the integral

ENGAGR.justification: a critical point where the derivative is zero and the mapping is neither strictly forward nor reverse

IFIX.justification: the permanent fixation of the new integration boundaries

phase_3.void_description: the pre-analytic state where no variable of integration is defined
phase_3.true_description: a valid transformation where the Jacobian is positive and limits are ordered
phase_3.false_description: an invalid transformation where the mapping is not one-to-one
phase_3.both_description: a transformation at a boundary where the mapping is singular yet the integral converges

steps.domain_action: establish the initial integral in the x-domain
identify the integrand and the differential dx
define the substitution function x = g(u)
branch the differential dx into the derivative g'(u) and the new differential du
verify the transformation is monotonic and orientation-preserving
compose the integrand with the substitution function to form f(g(u))
multiply the composed integrand by the derivative and differential to form the new integrand
calculate the inverse limits for the u-domain
fix the new limits of integration permanently
evaluate the integral to reach the terminal scalar value

phase_5.compiler_frontend: the substitution rule for definite integrals
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the sequential order of limit transformation and integrand substitution

phase_6.cycle_cost: computational effort of calculating the Jacobian determinant
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the total area under the curve is an invariant quantity
